name: Indonesia
visual_traits: layered foreground-to-background depth rather than flat single-plane composition
tolerance for high information density without it reading as clutter
hierarchy established by scale contrast more than by isolation
warm luminance from strong ambient daylight and deep shade
hand-drawn lettering heritage surviving inside digital typesetting
material honesty: surfaces show their making
communal framing — subjects rarely isolated from social context

social_values: deference to seniority and social position
hospitality as a form of respect
cultural_context.communication_style: High-context and indirect. Meaning is carried by warmth, framing and implication rather than by blunt assertion. Direct imperative commands read as rude; invitation and shared benefit read as persuasive. Visual communication follows the same logic — a claim is softened by context, and an offer is framed as something shared rather than something demanded.
cultural_context.spatial_philosophy: Indoor and outdoor are continuous rather than opposed. Thresholds, verandas and covered edges create layered transitional space instead of hard boundaries. Translated to a 2D surface this becomes permeable framing, overlapping planes and compositions that feel entered rather than viewed.

historical_influences.influence: Classical temple relief carving of Java and Sumatra
historical_influences.visual_consequence: Continuous horizontal narrative reading, dense low-relief surfaces where figure and ground interlock, and storytelling that unfolds along a band rather than resolving in a single frame. Expressed today as sequential, register-based composition and comfort with sustained detail across a horizontal axis.

historical_influences.influence: Islamic aniconic abstraction and calligraphic surface treatment
historical_influences.visual_consequence: Preference for abstraction, geometry and rhythmic repetition over figurative depiction in formal or civic contexts, plus a deep respect for lettering as an image in its own right. Expressed as typographic surfaces that carry meaning without illustration.

historical_influences.influence: Dutch colonial architecture and early European modernism adapted to the tropics
historical_influences.visual_consequence: Deep eaves, brise-soleil, high ceilings and shaded arcades — an aesthetic of managed light. Expressed as strong shadow structure, horizontal banding and a composition sensibility that treats shade as a positive element rather than an absence.

historical_influences.influence: Post-independence nation-building modernism and poster culture
historical_influences.visual_consequence: Bold condensed display lettering, monumental scale, optimistic geometry and high-contrast civic messaging. Expressed as confident headline dominance and a willingness to let type carry the whole surface.

historical_influences.influence: Reformasi-era street printing, activist screen printing and independent music graphics
historical_influences.visual_consequence: Raw registration, limited spot-colour printing, photocopy texture and hand-cut forms. Expressed as an accepted rough edge — imperfection reads as authenticity rather than as a defect.

historical_influences.influence: Modern tropical architecture and the independent café and craft economy
historical_influences.visual_consequence: Exposed concrete against warm timber, generous negative space, restrained earth palettes and a quiet, material-led premium language that coexists with the dense vernacular rather than replacing it.

composition.spatial_behavior: Layered rather than flat. Depth is built through overlapping planes, framing edges and foreground occlusion, echoing the veranda-and-threshold experience of built space. Compositions tolerate a busy periphery if the centre holds a clear focal claim, and they read comfortably from the centre outward.
composition.structure: Centred frontal address for authority and invitation; asymmetric layering for editorial and premium registers. Vertical stacking is natural because so much vernacular display space is tall and narrow. Hierarchy is carried by size jumps that are larger than European norms — a headline is expected to dominate decisively, not politely.

script_systems: Arabic-derived Pegon and Jawi (religious and traditional registers)
Javanese and Balinese scripts (ceremonial and place-identity registers)
relationships: one dominant display voice supported by a quiet neutral text face
large scale jumps between levels rather than subtle gradation
condensed display forms suited to tall narrow surfaces
hand-lettered warmth paired with neutral geometric sans for credibility
generous letterspacing in small supporting type to survive low-quality reproduction
typography.hierarchy_behavior: Three clear levels maximum in public-facing work: a decisive headline, a short qualifier, and a compact information block. Anything read at speed is expected to resolve in under two seconds, which pushes contrast between levels upward rather than toward refinement.
typography.notes: Custom and hand-painted lettering has never been displaced by typesetting; it migrated into it. Display type that carries a trace of the hand reads as local and trustworthy, while purely geometric neutrality reads as imported, corporate or premium. Both are legitimate — the choice is a positioning decision, not a quality one.

relationships: warm neutral base carrying one saturated accent
earth and clay tones against off-white and unbleached surfaces
deep shade greens read as natural rather than decorative
gold and deep green carry ceremonial and religious weight
high-chroma primaries belong to vernacular and mass-market registers
color.palette_logic: Two registers coexist. The vernacular register is high chroma and high contrast because it must survive sunlight, dust and distance. The contemporary premium register is warm-neutral and low chroma because it signals restraint against that noisy background. Choose the register deliberately — mixing them without intent produces work that reads as neither confident nor considered.
color.notes: Ambient daylight is intense and warm. Colours that look balanced on a calibrated screen often read washed out in the physical environments where the work is actually seen.

imagery.subject_treatment: People are shown in relation to others or to a place, rarely fully isolated. Warmth, ease and unforced expression read as authentic; posed perfection reads as advertising and is discounted accordingly. Hands, food, shared surfaces and gesture do a lot of communicative work.
imagery.framing: Medium and medium-close framing with visible environmental context. Full-bleed environmental shots with a small human presence establish place. Extreme isolation on seamless backgrounds reads as imported premium and should be a deliberate positioning choice.
imagery.lighting_bias: Strong directional daylight with real shadow structure, or diffused shade with warm bounce. Overcast neutrality feels foreign. Late-afternoon warmth is the most culturally legible light.

print_traditions: screen printing with limited spot colours
letterpress and stamp impression in official documents
materiality.notes: Surface texture is not decoration here; it is evidence of climate and making. Humidity, sun and dust age materials fast, so patina reads as normal rather than neglected. Perfectly clean digital surfaces can feel unrooted unless that sterility is the intended message.

graphic_language.shape_logic: Rounded and softened geometry in warm registers; hard rectilinear structure in civic and institutional ones. Interlocking figure-ground relationships feel more natural than isolated floating elements. Curves read as hospitable, sharp angles as official.
graphic_language.rhythm: Repetition with small variation rather than mechanical uniformity. Rhythm accumulates — a series of near-identical units reads as abundance and participation, which is why repetition is persuasive rather than monotonous in this context.
signage_traditions: tall narrow vertical banners at street edges
temporary event gateways and arch structures

contemporary_traits: specialty coffee and craft retail branding using restrained warm neutrals and generous space
modern tropical architecture pairing raw concrete with timber and planting
mobile-first vertical composition as the default rather than an adaptation
regional-pride typography and local-language wordplay used as a premium signal
creator-led product photography that favours evident realism over studio polish
religious and family calendar events driving major seasonal campaign rhythms

style_variants.name: Modern Tropical
style_variants.description: Restrained, material-led and quiet. Warm neutrals, exposed structural surfaces, generous negative space and a single confident type voice. Signals considered premium without importing a foreign visual identity.

style_variants.name: Urban Vernacular
style_variants.description: Dense, high-contrast and immediate. Condensed display lettering, saturated accents, layered information and a rough printed edge. Reads as local, energetic and honest about being commercial.

style_variants.name: Civic Modernist
style_variants.description: Monumental and optimistic. Bold condensed type, strong geometry, decisive scale jumps and a limited palette. Inherits the confidence of post-independence public communication without its period styling.

avoid_stereotypes.why: Applying a textile pattern as a background or border is the single most common shortcut to signalling this country, and it substitutes surface decoration for actual cultural reasoning. It also flattens a regionally specific craft into a generic texture.
avoid_stereotypes.instead: Carry the underlying logic — dense figure-ground interlock, rhythmic repetition with variation, and reserved negative space — into composition and shape language without reproducing a textile.

avoid_stereotypes.why: Shadow-puppet silhouettes are used as instant cultural shorthand in work that has nothing to do with the tradition, which reads as costume rather than identity.
avoid_stereotypes.instead: Use the structural ideas — dramatic silhouette, strong backlight, layered depth planes and narrative sequencing — as lighting and composition decisions.

avoid_stereotypes.why: Monument imagery imported into unrelated commercial work signals tourism, not brand, and immediately dates the piece to a heritage-campaign register.
avoid_stereotypes.instead: Draw on the relief tradition instead: horizontal narrative bands, stepped hierarchy and dense low-relief surface rhythm.

avoid_stereotypes.why: Terraced landscape imagery reduces a large and largely urban country to a single agricultural postcard, and it is almost never true to the audience being addressed.
avoid_stereotypes.instead: Use the contour logic — stepped horizontal registers, layered depth and graduated tonal bands — as a composition device.

avoid_stereotypes.why: Instrument imagery and its associated ornament are deployed as generic exotic seasoning, disconnected from the ceremonial contexts where they carry real meaning.
avoid_stereotypes.instead: Translate the musical structure — interlocking repeated cycles, layered rhythm at different speeds — into visual rhythm and pattern behaviour.

avoid_stereotypes.why: Traditional dress used as a costume signal in contemporary commercial work implies a heritage positioning the brand usually has not earned and does not want.
avoid_stereotypes.instead: Address formality and respect through posture, framing, colour restraint and typographic register instead of through costume.

avoid_stereotypes.why: The national emblem carries specific state and legal meaning; using it decoratively is both lazy and inappropriate outside official contexts.
avoid_stereotypes.instead: Signal national confidence through scale, civic typographic language and the optimism of post-independence public design.

avoid_stereotypes.why: The island-paradise framing is an outsider's tourism lens applied to a diverse, urban, fast-moving market, and domestic audiences read it as being sold to rather than spoken to.
avoid_stereotypes.instead: Ground the work in the actual visual environment of the audience — urban density, managed light, real materials and shared social space.

avoid_stereotypes.why: Generic ethnographic pattern flattens hundreds of distinct regional cultures into an undifferentiated texture and frequently misappropriates ceremonial forms.
avoid_stereotypes.instead: If a specific regional culture is genuinely relevant, name it, research it and let it inform structure. Otherwise leave it out.

avoid_stereotypes.why: Spice-trade imagery is a colonial-era framing of the region as a source of raw exotic goods, and it carries that history whether or not it is intended.
avoid_stereotypes.instead: If the subject is food, work from the contemporary eating environment — shared tables, hands, steam, everyday tableware.
